tasks.title: Speed up the overdue invoices query

pull.title: Add VAT to EU invoices
pull.author: sam-okafor
pull.body:
Invoices to EU customers now carry VAT at their country's standard rate. A business in another EU country is reverse charged, so its invoice carries none.

Adds Austria, Belgium, Spain, and Italy.

reviews.author: ana-ruiz
reviews.body: Looks right. One question on the reverse charge.

comments.author: ana-ruiz
comments.body: Should this check the customer's VAT number too? A business without one pays VAT like anyone else.

comments.author: sam-okafor
comments.body: Good catch. The checkout already refuses a business without a valid number, so it can't reach here, but I'll add a test that says so.

workspaceNotes.title: Conventions
workspaceNotes.body: Money is `Decimal`, never `float`. Every webhook body is signed with `sign()`.

turns.user: Webhook deliveries that get a 5xx are dropped. Retry server errors and connection failures with exponential backoff, up to five attempts. Don't retry a 4xx. Add tests.

events.text: The retry belongs in deliver(), so every caller gets it. A 4xx is the customer's endpoint refusing the event, so it stays final.

Done. `deliver()` now retries a 5xx or a connection error up to five attempts, waiting 0.5, 1, 2, and 4 seconds between them. A 4xx returns straight away.

- `backoff.py` is new and holds the delays.
- `deliver()` takes a `sleep` argument, so the tests run without waiting.
- Three new tests cover a retry that succeeds, giving up after five attempts, and a refusal.

All four tests pass.

turns.user: Does anything else call deliver() with arguments that would break?

tool.title: rg "deliver\(" billing
tool.output:
billing/scheduler/outbox.py:41:    ok = deliver(client, endpoint.url, event)
billing/webhooks/deliver.py:9:def deliver(client, url, event, sleep=time.sleep):

events.text:
One caller, the outbox scheduler, and it passes three positional arguments. `sleep` is new and last, with a default, so nothing breaks.

One thing to check: the scheduler gives each delivery 10 seconds, and five attempts can now take 7.5 seconds plus the requests. That fits, with little to spare.
